anomalies.obs: On the NAVC Peripherals sheet the BMI088 (U8) interface-strap pins are wired for SPI, not I2C: PS (pin 7) is tied to +3.3V (VDDIO), CSB2 (pin 5) is left as a no-connect, and SCL/SDI (pin 8) is connected to NET0036 while every other device on the same I2C bus (magnetometer U1, TMP100 U2, MPRLS U9, EEPROM U3) has its SCL on NET0038. Yet the same block is labelled 'I2C address: 0x19 (acc) / 0x69 (gyr)' and uses SCL/SDA net names.
anomalies.exp: The specification states the IMU is a 'Bosch BMI088, I2C addr 0x19 (acc) / 0x69 (gyr)' on the I2C bus. Per the BMI088 datasheet, PS tied to VDDIO selects SPI mode (PS must be tied to GND for I2C), CSB2 must be tied to VDDIO for I2C, and SCL must sit on the same bus net as the rest of the I2C devices (NET0038).

evidence.quote: NAVC Peripherals sheet, U8 BMI088: pin 7 PS -> +3.3V, pin 5 CSB2 -> X, pin 8 SCL/SDI -> NET0036, pin 9 SDA/SDO -> NET0040; block note 'I2C address: 0x19 (acc) / 0x69 (gyr)'
NAVC Peripherals sheet: U1 pin1 SCL/SPC -> NET0038, U2 pin2 SCL -> NET0038, U9 pin2 SCL/SCL -> NET0038, U3 pin1 SCL -> NET0038
IMU (accel + gyro) | NAVCPeripherals | Bosch BMI088, I2C addr 0x19 (acc) / 0x69 (gyr)

anomalies.impact: The strap pins put the BMI088 into SPI mode and isolate its SCL from the I2C bus, so the IMU will not acknowledge on the intended I2C address; the navigation computer loses accelerometer/gyro data, breaking state estimation and flight control.

parsed.summary: The drawing is internally inconsistent at the BMI088 (U8): it is declared and wired on an I2C bus (SCL/SDA labels, I2C address note, shared SDA net) but its interface-strap pins (PS to VDDIO, CSB2 floating, SCL on NET0036 instead of the bus net NET0038) select SPI and disconnect its clock, so the IMU would not communicate as intended. Other suspicious items (stale 'R1' note on the power sheet, the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap) are not behavioural deviations.
